summary: Uzbekistan's Foreign Ministry says foreign citizens need an entry visa except citizens of countries with a visa-free regime, which it lists — up to 30 days for countries including Australia, Canada, Japan, the Republic of Korea, New Zealand, the United Kingdom and the United States. It says citizens of the countries in its Appendix 1 can obtain an electronic visa at e-visa.gov.uz, for which the portal gives a fee of USD 20 for single entry; the portal tells nationals of countries not on that list to contact an Uzbek Foreign Ministry office abroad.

tips.text: The UK government says you must register with the local district OVIR within 3 days of your arrival, that hotel staff register guests, and that private hosts register you with their local OVIR or on the Emehmon system. Canada's travel advice says the registration slip may be requested upon leaving Uzbekistan.

The UK government says the import and use of drones in Uzbekistan is largely prohibited, that you must get a licence to import one and permission to use it before you arrive, and that without permission you can be fined or get a prison sentence.

The UK government says to change money only through official exchange booths and that it is illegal to change money on the black market, with harsh penalties. Canada's travel advice says you can exchange money at official exchange counters at international airports or at any bank and major hotel.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Uzbekistan?
faq.answer: Uzbekistan's Foreign Ministry lists the countries whose citizens have a visa-free regime, including Australia, Austria, Canada, Israel, Japan, Malaysia, New Zealand, the Republic of Korea, Switzerland, Türkiye, the United Kingdom and the United States (up to 30 days); the page was last updated on 1 June 2026. It lists countries whose citizens can obtain an electronic visa, among them Egypt, India, Thailand and Vietnam; the eVisa portal gives a fee of USD 20 for single entry and tells nationals of countries not on the list to contact an Uzbek Foreign Ministry office abroad.

faq.question: Do US citizens need a visa for Uzbekistan?
faq.answer: No. Uzbekistan's Foreign Ministry lists the United States of America under its visa-free regime of up to 30 days, and says that to stay more than 30 days a foreign citizen must obtain one of Uzbekistan's entry visas.

faq.question: How does the Uzbekistan eVisa work?
faq.answer: The eVisa portal says you apply online, uploading a facial photo and a copy of the passport data page, at least 3 working days before the planned date of arrival. The fee is USD 20 for single entry, USD 35 for double entry and USD 50 for multiple entry; applications are considered within 2 working days, the eVisa allows a stay of up to 30 days, and it is valid for entry within 90 days from the date of registration.

faq.question: Do I have to register my stay in Uzbekistan?
faq.answer: Yes. The UK government says you must register with the local district OVIR within 3 days of your arrival; hotel staff register guests, and private hosts register you with their local OVIR or on the Emehmon electronic system. It says that if you are unable to account for your whereabouts or fail to get registered, you could get a fine for each day that is missing or late and possibly be deported.

faq.question: How long can I stay in Uzbekistan visa-free?
faq.answer: Uzbekistan's Foreign Ministry says the 30-day and 60-day visa-free regimes run from the moment of crossing the state border. It lists Azerbaijan, Georgia, Armenia, Belarus, Kazakhstan, Moldova, Russia and Ukraine with a visa-free regime of unlimited duration, Tajikistan with up to 30 days and Kyrgyzstan with up to 60 days. The eVisa allows a stay of up to 30 days; for longer stays the Ministry says an entry visa is needed.
